summary: Autonomous ML experimentation loop: a coding agent proposes changes, runs a training job, keeps improvements (commits) and rolls back regressions — indefinitely. Released March 7 2026, 66K+ stars. Demonstrates a tight eval-loop pattern for self-improving agents.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — the accept/reject loop mirrors AgentForge's own review-and-revise cycle. Most directly relevant to extending plan repair (HID-186) with a metric-driven iteration step, but that issue already tracks partial retry. No new gap opened.

source: Trace2Skill: Distill Trajectory-Local Lessons into Transferable Agent Skills
summary: Framework that distills agent execution traces into a portable skill using parallel analyst sub-agents; distilled skills generalise to held-out and out-of-distribution tasks. Complementary to existing distillation approaches.
relevanceToAgentForge: High — AgentForge ships skill distillation (distillationAgent.ts, agentSkillRepository.ts) but the executor prompt does not yet receive distilled skills (noted gap in CLAUDE.md). Trace2Skill's parallel-analyst consolidation pattern could improve distillation quality. Blocked by backlog cap this run.

source: ClawTrace: Cost-Aware Tracing for LLM Agent Skill Distillation
summary: Cost-aware execution trace tracing system for skill distillation; selects which trace segments to distil based on token cost, reducing distillation overhead.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — relevant once HID-163 (telemetry) ships; cost-aware trace selection is only meaningful when per-stage cost data exists. Too early now.

source: SKILL-KD: Contrastive Skill Distillation for LLM Agents
summary: Uses teacher-student behavioural contrast as the primary signal and iterative refinement of candidate skill patches until they demonstrably shift student behaviour. Treats distillation as an adaptive search.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — a more principled alternative to AgentForge's current single-pass distillation. Could improve skill quality but requires multi-agent panel (rejected as cost multiplier). Deferred.

source: State of AI Agent Memory 2026 (mem0.ai report)
summary: Industry survey of agent memory architectures in 2026: episodic, semantic, and procedural tiers; cross-session persistence challenges (identity resolution, staleness). Anthropic Dreaming primitive noted as async background consolidation.
relevanceToAgentForge: High — cross-run episodic memory is already tracked by HID-188. No new gap. The async-consolidation pattern (Dreaming) could inform HID-188 implementation once it opens.

summary: Super-agent harness that orchestrates sub-agents, memory, sandboxes, and extensible skills; v2.0 topped GitHub Trending. Addresses weak memory, poor task decomposition, and brittle tool use in long workflows.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — DeerFlow's architecture is multi-agent/parallel, which AgentForge deliberately defers. Task decomposition is tracked by HID-10. No verified new gap.

source: LangGraph vs CrewAI vs AutoGen 2026 framework comparison
summary: Comprehensive comparison of the three dominant agent orchestration frameworks in 2026. LangGraph dominates enterprise; CrewAI for rapid prototyping; AutoGen AG2 with event-driven async core.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — AgentForge uses a custom state machine deliberately. Framework comparisons are informational but open no verified gap.

source: Self-Improving Agents in 2026: 9 Open-Source Frameworks (Turing Post)
summary: Overview of nine open-source self-improvement frameworks including Hermes, Gödel Agent, HyperAgents, and Prime Agent (released Aug 5 2026). All feature persistent memory, reflection loops, or self-generated training data.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — reflection/self-improvement overlaps with HID-186 (partial retry) and HID-188 (episodic memory). No new verified gap beyond tracked issues. RL training loops and prompt self-evolution are explicitly red-flagged in Phase 3.

summary: September 2026 GitHub trending summary: autonomous agents, domain-specific skill libraries, MCP tooling, and visual agent builders (Langflow, Dify, Flowise) dominate. Google ADK and Harmonist also noted.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — ecosystem trend data. Domain-specific skill libraries are the most relevant signal but AlreadyForge tracks this via skill distillation. No new gap.
